content: The interpretation of collected defect data is challenging due to the diverse sources of information, including randomized trials with limited pregnancy outcomes, observational studies, registries, case reports, and adverse event reporting systems. These sources vary in their biases and methods of reporting and evaluating defects. Most studies focus on live births and do not include data on stillbirths or pregnancy terminations. In the APR and NSHPC databases, no neural tube defects (NTDs) were reported. This defect, characterized by ventriculomegaly and abnormal cortical folding, was considered a neuronal migration disorder of unknown etiology. One NTD was reported in the ViiV post-marketing database, which appears to overlap with the FDA database. This case involved an infant born to an HIV-positive woman in Namibia who started DTG preconception. Fetal abnormalities consistent with NTD were identified on serial ultrasounds during the second trimester, but the pregnancy outcome (termination or live birth) was not available. The WHO Vigibase reported no CNS defects, while the FDA database reported one NTD without a denominator, likely overlapping with the ViiV database. Several ongoing and planned studies aim to provide additional data on this issue. These include randomized controlled trials (RCTs) such as DOLPHIN-2, VESTED, and ADVANCE, as well as surveillance studies like the Tsepamo study in Botswana. Retrospective cases reported to the APR are considered less reliable than prospective cases due to reporting biases. These cases highlight the importance of prospective data collection for accurate assessment. One case involved a 29-year-old woman on DTG who continued her pregnancy after anencephaly was diagnosed on ultrasound. Another case involved a 23-year-old woman with a history of seizures who delivered an infant with a sacral meningocele. Both cases will be included in future APR updates. In summary, while no NTDs have been reported in prospective APR data for DTG, retrospective and post-marketing data suggest isolated cases of concern.
